rounds.text: Sunrakshakk Industries is materially under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by its exceptional compounding fundamentals that starkly outpace its modest P/E multiple of 20.5x [E1]. The business is scaling at an extraordinary rate, delivering compounded sales growth of 140% and compounded profit growth of 138% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This top-line and bottom-line surge is backed by stellar capital efficiency, highlighted by a robust ROE of 24.33% to 29.6% and an ROCE reaching up to 29.2%, both comfortably outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E13]. Furthermore, the company commands a solid balance sheet with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.24x and comfortable short-term liquidity through a current ratio of 2.01x [E29, E30]. Operational improvements are well underway, notably demonstrated by debtor days dropping sharply from 51.8 to 30.3 days [E44]. Management's clear strategic vision targets approximately INR1,000 crores in revenue by FY28 through existing capacities without major new capex, while working toward a 7% PAT margin [E54, E56, E61]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -34 Cr with a cash conversion of -0.97x in Mar 2026, and the dividend yield remains at 0.00% [E4, E26, E27].

Conceded: [E14], [E15]. Despite impressive top-line and profit growth metrics, the fundamental quality of this growth is deeply undermined by severe cash-flow destruction. Operating cash flow for Mar 2026 plunged to Rs -34 Cr, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.97x, while free cash flow deteriorated even further to Rs -92 Cr [E26, E27, E28]. This stark divergence between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation raises serious governance and operational questions, amplified by explicit flags that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E46]. Furthermore, operating margins have been on a multi-year downward trend, falling by 7 percentage points over the last three years to 9% in the TTM [E22, E24]. Valuation multiples also reflect a rich pricing environment with EV/EBITDA at 13.54x and P/B at 5x, both sitting well above sector benchmarks [E7, E11]. Finally, despite continuous profitability, the company stubbornly distributes a dividend yield of 0.00%, offering shareholders zero cash return while management faces pressure on pricing [E4, E45, E72].

The bear’s focus on cash flow ignores the company’s strategic decision to prioritize aggressive expansion and capacity utilization, which explains the temporary negative cash flow [E26, E27, E28]. The capital raised through the preferential issue was specifically earmarked for these growth initiatives, including manufacturing capacity and working capital, rather than being a sign of operational failure [E69, E70, E71]. While the bear highlights margin compression, it overlooks that EBITDA margins have already begun to recover, expanding from 9.31% in Q3 FY26 to 10.19% in Q4 FY26 due to operating leverage [E63, E65]. Conceded: [E46]. Regarding valuation, the bear ignores that the company’s superior ROE of 29.6% and ROCE of 29.2% significantly outperform sector benchmarks, justifying a premium over peers with lower efficiency [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Finally, the absence of dividends is a deliberate choice to reinvest in the business to reach the stated revenue aspiration of ₹1,000 crores by FY28, a goal supported by existing capacity that requires no major further capex [E54, E61, E74].

The bull characterizes negative cash flow as a strategic choice, yet the evidence shows a severe disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation, with operating cash flow at a deeply negative Rs -34 Cr and free cash flow at Rs -92 Cr [E26, E27, E28]. While the bull claims capital raises support growth, the company’s operating margin trend has been decreasing over the last four years, suggesting that these investments have yet to translate into sustainable operational efficiency [E24]. Conceded: [E69, E70, E71]. Although the bull points to a quarterly margin recovery, this ignores the broader reality that the yearly operating margin has compressed by 7 percentage points over three years, and the quarterly trend remains inconsistent [E22, E25]. The bull justifies a valuation premium based on ROE and ROCE, but it fails to address that the company trades at a P/E of 20.55x and a P/B of 5x, both of which are significantly higher than their respective sector benchmarks of 4.99x and 2.56x [E6, E7, E9, E13]. Finally, the bull’s reliance on a future revenue target of ₹1,000 crores by FY28 ignores management's own admission that forward-looking statements are subject to significant risks, including competitive pressures and macroeconomic trends [E54, E73, E74].

evidence.quote: As shared earlier, our medium-term aspirations remain to achieve approximately INR1,000 crores in revenue by FY28.

evidence.fact: The company expects an organic growth of 10% to 15% every year over and above the annualized run rate of INR800 crores.
evidence.quote: And we are expecting organic growth of 10%-15% on every year basis, that is point number one.

evidence.fact: Management aims to achieve a profit after tax (PAT) margin of 7% in the near future.
evidence.quote: We are, we have taken an internal target of achieving PAT at the rate 7% in the near future, and we are working on it.

evidence.fact: Management stated that India's FMCG sector continues to offer attractive long-term growth potential.
evidence.quote: India's FMCG sector continues to offer attractive long-term growth potential supported by rising consumption, increasing penetration, and growing demand across categories.

evidence.fact: Personal care and home care are the categories currently contributing substantially to the FMCG business.
evidence.quote: In the FMCG category, both in the personal care and home care, these two are the categories which are contributing substantially as of now.

evidence.fact: Consolidated revenue grew in Q4 FY26 supported by healthy demand across personal care, home-care, FMCG intermediates, and Edible’s categories.
evidence.quote: In Q4 FY26, consolidated revenue increased by 92.32% YoY to ₹197.59 crore, supported by healthy demand across personal care, home-care, FMCG intermediates, and Edible’s categories.

evidence.fact: The Guwahati facility was successfully commissioned and revamped, enhancing capabilities in soap noodles and cosmetics.
evidence.quote: The successful commissioning and revamp of our Guwahati facility has enhanced our capabilities in soap noodles and cosmetics while improving our reach in the Northeast and other adjacent markets.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the INR1,000 crores revenue target can be achieved using existing capacities without major capex investments.
evidence.quote: So this INR1,000 crores turnover can be achieved with the existing capacity and we don't see much of the expansion or investment in the capex side for achieving this INR1,000 crores topline.

evidence.fact: The Bhilwara facility became fully operational with monthly capacities of 850 MT in savories and 650 MT in spices.
evidence.quote: • Entry into Edibles: Bhilwara facility became fully operational with monthly capacities of 850 MT in savories and 650 MT in spices, contributing since September 2025.

evidence.fact: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin increased to 10.19% compared to 9.31% in Q3 FY26.
evidence.quote: Importantly, profitability improved during the quarter with EBITDA margin increasing to 10.19% in Q4 FY26 from 9.31% in Q3 FY26, while PAT margin improved to 6.12% from 5.74%.

evidence.fact: Management noted that year-over-year EBITDA and PAT margins went down mainly because of the product mix.
evidence.quote: So the Y-o-Y EBITDA and PAT margin went down just because of the product mix.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margin expanded to 10.19% in Q4 FY26 from 9.31% in Q3 FY26 due to operating leverage and improving capacity utilization.
evidence.quote: Importantly, despite FMCG contributing the majority of revenues, profitability continued to improve, with EBITDA margin expanding to 10.19% in Q4 FY26 from 9.31% in Q3 FY26 and PAT margin improving to 6.12% from 5.74%.

evidence.fact: Sunrakshakk operates a manufacturing network across Bhilwara, Roorkee, and Guwahati, combined with a customer base of over 200 customers.
evidence.quote: Our manufacturing network across Bhilwara, Roorkee, and Guwahati combined with a customer base of over 200 customers provides a strong foundation for our future growth.

evidence.fact: Cosmetics capacity utilization at the Guwahati plant is around 45% to 50%.
evidence.quote: So in our Guwahati unit, the cosmetics segment we are utilizing our capacity at around 45% to 50% for Guwahati.

evidence.fact: Total FMCG and FMCG intermediary chemicals capacity stands at 19,640 tons per month.
evidence.quote: 19,640 Tons pm (FMCG & FMCG Intermediary Chemicals)

evidence.fact: The successful capital raise through the preferential issue strengthened the balance sheet and enhanced the ability to invest in manufacturing capacity and working capital.
evidence.quote: Another important development during the year was the successful capital raise through the preferential issue. The fundraised has strengthened our balance sheet and enhanced our ability to invest in manufacturing capacity, working capital requirement, and future growth opportunities.

evidence.fact: Out of the preferential issue proceeds, approximately INR55 crores was utilized for the FMCG segment and the rest for the edible section, with INR10 crores held in a fixed deposit.
evidence.quote: So out of that preferential, most of the fund is being utilized for expanding our manufacturing facility in edible category and the FMCG Guwahati unit. Remaining amount is, and if I say, 55 tentatively, INR55 crores we had utilized for FMCG segment and rest I believe 10, our INR10 crores FD is available with us and remaining amount we had used for edible section.

evidence.fact: The company raised ₹98.65 crore to support expansion and the acquisition of Sunrakshak Agro Products Pvt. Ltd.
evidence.quote: • Robust Growth: Achieved highest-ever consolidated turnover and raised ₹98.65 crore to support expansion.

evidence.fact: Management noted a bit of pressure on pricing at the end of Quarter 4 and the beginning of Q1 FY26, though supplies faced no challenges.
evidence.quote: So definitely there was a bit pressure in terms of pricing during the end of the Quarter 4 and the beginning of Q1 FY26. With regard to supplies, we don't force or we didn't face any challenges.

evidence.fact: Management noted that forward-looking statements are subject to risks including general market, macro-economic, governmental and regulatory trends.
evidence.quote: These factors include, but are not limited to, general market, macro-economic, governmental and regulatory trends, movements in currency exchange and interest rates, competitive pressures, technological developments, changes in the financial conditions of third parties dealing with us, legislative developments, and other key factors that could affect our business and financial performance.

evidence.quote: As shared earlier, our medium-term aspirations remain to achieve approximately INR1,000 crores in revenue by FY28.
